decisions.reason: The referral-code identity transferred on resale is already explicitly represented by the candidate's same-message introduction; adding the mint number to NFT metadata does not alter the transfer behavior.
The candidate's same-message introduction already states that each NFT's mint number is its permanent referral code and that it appears in on-chain NFT metadata.
The metadata source of the referral-code attribute does not change the unlimited-mint collection model.
Referral-code metadata identity does not change the enabled, flat $10 secondary-sale royalty.
The FAQ's same-message introduction already states both that the mint number is the permanent referral code and that the code appears in on-chain NFT metadata.
Defining the referral code as the NFT's mint number does not alter the commission amount, trigger, recipient, destination, timing, or limit.
The referral-code metadata attribute does not change badge milestones, award conditions, or on-chain badge recording.
Adding referral-code identity to NFT metadata does not change either prize-ticket counter or its reset behavior.
The identity of a referral code does not change allocation behavior when no referral code is supplied.
The referral code's mint-number identity does not change ticket issuance quantities, recipient, cycles, or secondary-sale exclusion.
The referral-code metadata source does not change the mint price or any revenue-allocation amount or destination.
Referral-code identity in NFT metadata does not change the manual one-click prize claim flow or its Winners-page location.
